'''''From Russia with Love''''' is a 2005 [[Third-person shooter|third-person shooter game]] developed by [[Visceral Games|EA Redwood Shores]] and published by [[Electronic Arts]] (EA). It is based on the [[From Russia with Love (film)|1963 ''James Bond'' film of the same name]] but with several changes, including additional characters, locations, and a different villainous organisation. Additionally, it features elements of later Bond films such as the [[Aston Martin DB5]] that debuted in ''[[Goldfinger (film)|Goldfinger]]'' (1964) and the [[jet pack]] from ''[[Thunderball (film)|Thunderball]]'' (1965).

''From Russia with Love'' is notable in that it is the only video game to use [[Sean Connery]]'s younger likeness as [[James Bond]] and the first to include all new voice work by the actor after twenty-two years away from the role,<ref name=Perry/> marking his eighth and final performance as Bond across any medium before his death in 2020. ''From Russia with Love'' is also the last James Bond video game developed or published by Electronic Arts before they lost the rights to [[Activision]] in 2006.

''From Russia with Love'' was released for [[GameCube]], [[PlayStation 2]], and [[Xbox (console)|Xbox]] in November 2005. A [[PlayStation Portable]] (PSP) version was released in April 2006. The game received mixed reviews from critics.

== Gameplay ==
[[File:From Russia with Love video game screenshot.jpg|thumb|left|Third-person view of Bond|alt=A man in a suit holding a gun. It is snowing, and a factory is on the background. On the bottom corners icons indicating ammo and health of the player can be seen.]]
''From Russia with Love'' is primarily a [[third-person shooter]], with the player taking on the role of James Bond. The game is played across 14 main levels but includes four bonus levels which can be unlocked throughout. The player has mission objectives that must be carried out before proceeding to the next level.<ref name=Perry/>

The game includes several driving levels, in which the player takes control of various armed vehicles and must evade enemies, using weapons such as a [[machine gun]] and rockets. [[Motorboat|Speedboats]] and Bond's [[Aston Martin DB5]] are among the armed vehicles used by the player.<ref name=Chest>{{cite web |last=Perry |first=Douglass C. |title=James Bond's Weapon Chest |url=https://www.ign.com/articles/2005/09/15/james-bonds-weapon-chest |website=IGN |access-date=2021-12-22 |date=2005-09-14 |archive-date=19 November 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211119163817/https://www.ign.com/articles/2005/09/15/james-bonds-weapon-chest |url-status=live }}</ref> Jet packs, equipped with machine guns and rockets, are also used throughout the game.<ref name=Chest/>

[[File:From Russia with Love game screenshot.jpg|thumb|left|Bond using the jet pack]]
On foot, Bond can jump across certain designated ledges. He can use his usual [[Walther PP#PPK|Walther PPK]], in addition to other weapons such as [[shotgun]]s, [[assault rifle]]s, [[sniper rifle]]s, [[bazooka]]s, and [[grenade]]s. He can also engage in hand-to-hand combat with enemies. Points can be collected throughout the game, by killing enemies in specific ways, or by collecting [[schematic]]s hidden in each level. Such points can be used to upgrade weapons, or unlock bonus content such as concept art and behind-the-scene movies.<ref name=Perry>{{cite web |last=Perry |first=Douglass C. |title=From Russia With Love |url=https://www.ign.com/articles/2005/10/27/from-russia-with-love-5 |website=[[IGN]] |access-date=2021-12-22 |date=2005-10-26 |archive-date=19 November 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211119163821/https://www.ign.com/articles/2005/10/27/from-russia-with-love-5 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name=Preview>{{cite web |last=Torres |first=Ricardo |title=From Russia With Love Preview |url=https://www.gamespot.com/articles/from-russia-with-love-preview/1100-6135749/ |website=[[GameSpot]] |access-date=2021-12-22 |date=2005-10-18 |archive-date=19 November 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211119164523/https://www.gamespot.com/articles/from-russia-with-love-preview/1100-6135749/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

A variety of [[Q (James Bond)|Q]] gadgets are used throughout the game, including a rappelling gun that is used to climb and descend to new areas. A laser wristwatch is used to penetrate [[bulletproof glass]] and destroy control panels, thereby unlocking security doors that block the player's path. Mini helicopters are used to access remote areas and can be detonated, also to destroy certain control panels. Sonic [[cufflink]]s can be used to emit a high-frequency that temporarily incapacitates enemies. A serum gun can be used to inject enemies from afar, confusing them into turning against their own. In addition, there are instances where the player must equip a [[gas mask]] to proceed through rooms that become filled with toxins.<ref name=Gadgets>{{cite web |title=From Russia With Love Gadgets Spotlight |url=https://www.gamespot.com/articles/from-russia-with-love-gadgets-spotlight/1100-6133305/ |website=GameSpot |access-date=2021-12-22 |date=2005-09-15 |archive-date=19 November 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211119170845/https://www.gamespot.com/articles/from-russia-with-love-gadgets-spotlight/1100-6133305/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

The game includes an offline [[Multiplayer video game|multiplayer]] option,<ref name=Preview/> with various gameplay modes, characters, and locations. It supports up to four players.<ref name=Perry/><ref>{{cite web |last=Perry |first=Douglass C. |title=From Russia With Love: Multiplayer Madness |url=https://www.ign.com/articles/2005/10/14/from-russia-with-love-multiplayer-madness-2 |website=IGN |access-date=2021-12-22 |date=2005-10-14 |archive-date=19 November 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211119164511/https://www.ign.com/articles/2005/10/14/from-russia-with-love-multiplayer-madness-2 |url-status=live }}</ref>

The [[PlayStation Portable]] (PSP) version plays largely the same as the home-console versions, although it includes [[minigame]]s and new multiplayer levels and characters, but removes the driving missions.<ref>{{cite web |last=Castro |first=Juan |title=From Russia with Love First Impressions |url=https://www.ign.com/articles/2006/01/20/from-russia-with-love-first-impressions |website=IGN |access-date=2021-12-22 |date=2006-01-20 |archive-date=19 November 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211119163820/https://www.ign.com/articles/2006/01/20/from-russia-with-love-first-impressions |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Castro |first=Juan |title=From Russia with Love Impressions |url=https://www.ign.com/articles/2006/02/08/from-russia-with-love-impressions |website=IGN |access-date=2021-12-22 |date=2006-02-08 |archive-date=19 November 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211119164524/https://www.ign.com/articles/2006/02/08/from-russia-with-love-impressions |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Castro |first=Juan |title=From Russia with Love: The Villains |url=https://www.ign.com/articles/2006/02/23/from-russia-with-love-the-villains |website=IGN |access-date=2021-12-22 |date=2006-02-23 |archive-date=19 November 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211119163820/https://www.ign.com/articles/2006/02/23/from-russia-with-love-the-villains |url-status=live }}</ref>

== Plot ==
One of the changes to the plot of the video game is the absence of the villainous organisation [[SPECTRE]], who played a vital role in the film. Due to legal issues that had plagued the James Bond film series since 1963, the organization was renamed "OCTOPUS" and appears to lack a central leader in the same vein as [[Ernst Stavro Blofeld]]. The SPECTRE name was tied up in a long-running dispute over the film rights to ''[[Thunderball (film)|Thunderball]]'' (1965), between [[United Artists]]/[[Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer|MGM]] and the now-deceased screenwriter [[Kevin McClory]].<ref>{{cite web |title=James Bond's New Enemies? |url=https://www.ign.com/articles/2005/10/24/james-bonds-new-enemies |website=IGN |access-date=2021-12-22 |date=2005-10-24 |archive-date=22 December 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211222222933/https://www.ign.com/articles/2005/10/24/james-bonds-new-enemies |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Freiberg |first=Chris |title=15 Best James Bond 007 Games Ever |url=https://www.denofgeek.com/games/best-james-bond-007-games-ever/ |website=[[Den of Geek]] |access-date=2021-12-22 |date=2021-09-30 |archive-date=25 October 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211025213714/https://www.denofgeek.com/games/best-james-bond-007-games-ever/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

The game begins with a pre-title sequence in which Elizabeth Stark, the [[Prime Minister of the United Kingdom]]'s daughter, is kidnapped by OCTOPUS while attending a party. Bond was assigned to attend the party for just such an event, and he defeats OCTOPUS and rescues Miss Stark.

Similar to the film, OCTOPUS has conceived a plan to embarrass [[MI6|British Secret Service]] agent 007 for the death of Dr. [[Julius No]] from the film ''[[Dr. No (film)|Dr. No]]'' (1962), in which No was an agent of SPECTRE. The plan involves the theft of a [[Soviet Union|Soviet]] encoding machine known as the Lektor with the help of a defecting Soviet agent, Tatiana Romanova. However, Romanova is being used by OCTOPUS to lure James Bond into a trap; their ultimate goal is to let him obtain the Lektor and then ambush him for it, killing him in a humiliating fashion as well. Romanova is sent by Rosa Klebb, an agent of the KGB (in both the novel and film, an agent of SMERSH) who has secretly defected to OCTOPUS. Her immediate subordinate, Donald "Red" Grant, protects Bond through the first half of the game and attacks him in the second. The game ends with a final assault on OCTOPUS headquarters, during which Grant is fatally shot by Bond.

== Development and release ==
''From Russia with Love'' is based on the 1963 [[From Russia with Love (film)|film of the same name]]. The game adaptation was written by [[Bruce Feirstein]], who previously worked on the scripts for the Bond films ''[[GoldenEye]]'' (1995), ''[[Tomorrow Never Dies]]'' (1997) and ''[[The World Is Not Enough]]'' (1999), in addition to the video game ''[[James Bond 007: Everything or Nothing]]'' (2004).<ref>{{cite web |last=Robinson |first=Martin |title=Playing as 007: Bringing Bond to Games |url=https://www.ign.com/articles/2010/11/04/playing-as-007-bringing-bond-to-games |website=IGN |access-date=2021-12-22 |date=2010-11-04 |archive-date=23 December 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211223000102/https://www.ign.com/articles/2010/11/04/playing-as-007-bringing-bond-to-games |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Dayus |first=Oscar |title=Exploring James Bond's Uneven Video Game History |url=https://www.gamespot.com/articles/exploring-james-bonds-uneven-video-game-history/1100-6464744/ |website=GameSpot |access-date=2021-12-22 |date=2019-02-12 |archive-date=23 December 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211223000106/https://www.gamespot.com/articles/exploring-james-bonds-uneven-video-game-history/1100-6464744/ |url-status=live }}</ref> [[Electronic Arts]] (EA) announced the game in January 2005.<ref>{{cite web |last=Perry |first=Douglass C. |title=From Florida With Love |url=https://www.ign.com/articles/2005/02/01/from-florida-with-love |website=IGN |access-date=2021-12-09 |date=2005-01-31 |archive-date=19 November 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211119164520/https://www.ign.com/articles/2005/02/01/from-florida-with-love |url-status=live }}</ref> EA had spent more than two years developing an [[Game engine|engine]] for the game, and nearly a year was spent on pre-production.<ref>{{cite web |last=Casamassina |first=Matt |title=E3 2005: James Bond 007: From Russia with Love |url=https://www.ign.com/articles/2005/05/20/e3-2005-james-bond-007-from-russia-with-love |website=IGN |access-date=2021-12-21 |date=2005-05-19 |archive-date=19 November 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211119163816/https://www.ign.com/articles/2005/05/20/e3-2005-james-bond-007-from-russia-with-love |url-status=live }}</ref> The development team included members who had previously worked on ''Everything or Nothing'',<ref name=Perry1/> also a third-person game. The gameplay in ''From Russia with Love'' is similar to the earlier game.<ref name=Navarro/>

The game's executive producer, [[Glen Schofield]], considered 1963's ''From Russia with Love'' to be among the most popular [[List of James Bond films|Bond films]].<ref name=Perry1>{{cite web |last=Perry |first=Douglass C. |title=From Russia With Love |url=https://www.ign.com/articles/2005/04/29/from-russia-with-love-9 |website=IGN |access-date=2021-12-21 |date=2005-04-29 |archive-date=19 November 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211119163833/https://www.ign.com/articles/2005/04/29/from-russia-with-love-9 |url-status=live }}</ref> EA described the game as a [[director's cut]], as it offers additional story elements, locations, and [[gadget]]s compared to the film.<ref name=Adams/><ref name=GSpy/><ref>{{cite web |last=Adams |first=David |title=From Russia With Official Love |url=https://www.ign.com/articles/2005/04/28/from-russia-with-official-love |website=IGN |access-date=2021-12-09 |date=2005-04-28 |archive-date=19 November 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211119164529/https://www.ign.com/articles/2005/04/28/from-russia-with-official-love |url-status=live }}</ref> Some concepts from later Bond films were incorporated into the game, including Bond's Aston Martin DB5, which debuted in ''[[Goldfinger (film)|Goldfinger]]'' (1964);<ref name=Virtue/> and the jet pack,<ref name=Torres>{{cite web |last=Torres |first=Ricardo |title=From Russia With Love First Look |url=https://www.gamespot.com/articles/from-russia-with-love-first-look/1100-6123078/ |website=[[GameSpot]] |access-date=2021-12-22 |date=2005-04-28 |archive-date=19 November 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211119164535/https://www.gamespot.com/articles/from-russia-with-love-first-look/1100-6123078/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name=OXM/> which was introduced in ''[[Thunderball (film)|Thunderball]]'' (1965).<ref>{{cite web |last=Bramwell |first=Tom |title=From Russia With a Jetpack? |url=https://www.eurogamer.net/articles/news180405fromrussiawithlove |website=[[Eurogamer]] |access-date=2021-12-21 |date=2005-04-18 |archive-date=21 December 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211221180904/https://www.eurogamer.net/articles/news180405fromrussiawithlove |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name=Navarro>{{cite web |last=Navarro |first=Alex |title=From Russia With Love E3 2005 Hands-On |url=https://www.gamespot.com/articles/from-russia-with-love-e3-2005-hands-on/1100-6125662/ |website=GameSpot |access-date=2021-12-22 |date=2005-05-23 |archive-date=19 November 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211119163806/https://www.gamespot.com/articles/from-russia-with-love-e3-2005-hands-on/1100-6125662/ |url-status=live }}</ref> ''Everything or Nothing'' had featured a mechanical spider gadget known as the Q Spider, although the development team considered it too modern for ''From Russia with Love'', opting instead for the Q Copter.<ref>{{cite web |last=Mirabella III |first=Fran |title=GC 2005: James Bond 007: From Russia with Love |url=https://www.ign.com/articles/2005/08/20/gc-2005-james-bond-007-from-russia-with-love |website=IGN |access-date=2021-12-22 |date=2005-08-20 |archive-date=19 November 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211119163825/https://www.ign.com/articles/2005/08/20/gc-2005-james-bond-007-from-russia-with-love |url-status=live }}</ref>

[[Sean Connery]] reprised his role from the film as James Bond, lending his voice to the game. His likeness, from 1963, was also implemented.<ref name=Adams/><ref name=Thorsen/> The game marked Connery's first appearance as Bond since the film ''[[Never Say Never Again]]'' (1983), and it also served as his video game debut.<ref name=Gold>{{cite web |last=Thorsen |first=Tor |title=From Russia With Love given gold finger |url=https://www.gamespot.com/articles/from-russia-with-love-given-gold-finger/1100-6136207/ |website=GameSpot |access-date=2021-12-22 |date=2005-10-20 |archive-date=19 November 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211119165310/https://www.gamespot.com/articles/from-russia-with-love-given-gold-finger/1100-6136207/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Connery said, "As an artist, I see this as another way to explore the creative process. Video games are an extremely popular form of entertainment today, and I am looking forward to seeing how it all fits together".<ref name=Adams/> Two factors led to his participation in the project: ''From Russia with Love'' was his favorite Bond film, and his grandchildren were avid video game players.<ref name=Lipsey/> Connery recorded his lines from his home in [[the Bahamas]].<ref name=Garratt/><ref name=Lipsey>{{cite web |last=Lipsey |first=Sid |title=Review: Connery brings Bond back to the U.S.S.R. |url=http://www.cnn.com/2005/TECH/fun.games/11/10/bond.rwl/ |website=[[CNN]] |access-date=2021-12-22 |date=2005-11-10 |archive-date=22 December 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211222190617/http://www.cnn.com/2005/TECH/fun.games/11/10/bond.rwl/ |url-status=live }}</ref> His character model was based primarily on frames from the film.<ref name=GSpy>{{cite web |title=Interviews: From Russia With Love |url=http://cube.gamespy.com/gamecube/james-bond-007-from-russia-with-love/654415p1.html |website=GameSpy |access-date=2021-12-22 |date=2005-09-29 |pages=1–2 |archive-date=18 March 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120318010130/http://cube.gamespy.com/gamecube/james-bond-007-from-russia-with-love/654415p1.html |url-status=live }}</ref> The game's use of physical combat was inspired by Connery's portrayal of Bond in the films,<ref name=Torres/> with Schofield describing him as "more of a brawler" compared to later actors who played the character.<ref name=Byrd/>

The likenesses of several deceased actors from the film were used as well, including [[Desmond Llewelyn]] as [[Q (James Bond)|Q]], [[Robert Shaw (actor)|Robert Shaw]] as Red Grant, and [[Lotte Lenya]] as [[Rosa Klebb]].<ref name=Adams>{{cite web |last=Adams |first=David |title=Sean Connery Back as Bond |url=https://www.ign.com/articles/2005/04/05/sean-connery-back-as-bond |website=IGN |access-date=2021-12-09 |date=2005-04-05 |archive-date=19 November 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211119164518/https://www.ign.com/articles/2005/04/05/sean-connery-back-as-bond |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name=Thorsen>{{cite web |last=Thorsen |first=Tor |title=Connery confirms From Russia With Love role |url=https://www.gamespot.com/articles/connery-confirms-from-russia-with-love-role/1100-6121767/ |website=GameSpot |access-date=2021-12-09 |date=2005-04-06 |archive-date=19 November 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211119164539/https://www.gamespot.com/articles/connery-confirms-from-russia-with-love-role/1100-6121767/ |url-status=live }}</ref> The game also introduces two new characters: [[Natasha Bedingfield]] as Elizabeth Stark,<ref name=Bedingfield/><ref name=Garratt>{{cite web |last=Garratt |first=Patrick |title=Natasha Bedingfield: EA's latest Bond girl |url=https://www.eurogamer.net/articles/i_natashabedingfield |website=Eurogamer |access-date=2021-12-22 |date=2005-11-08 |archive-date=22 December 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211222182257/https://www.eurogamer.net/articles/i_natashabedingfield |url-status=live }}</ref> and [[Maria Menounos]] as Eva.<ref>{{cite web |last=Surette |first=Tim |title=From Russia With Love Bond girl confirmed |url=https://www.gamespot.com/articles/from-russia-with-love-bond-girl-confirmed/1100-6130249/ |website=GameSpot |access-date=2021-12-22 |date=2005-08-03 |archive-date=19 November 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211119170831/https://www.gamespot.com/articles/from-russia-with-love-bond-girl-confirmed/1100-6130249/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Casamassina |first=Matt |title=Bond Girl Named |url=https://www.ign.com/articles/2005/08/03/bond-girl-named |website=IGN |access-date=2021-12-22 |date=2005-08-03 |archive-date=19 November 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211119163829/https://www.ign.com/articles/2005/08/03/bond-girl-named |url-status=live }}</ref> Bedingfield had previously performed a song for the Bond spin-off game ''[[GoldenEye: Rogue Agent]]'' (2004).<ref name=Bedingfield>{{cite web |title=Bedingfield 'bonds' with EA? |url=https://www.gamespot.com/articles/bedingfield-bonds-with-ea/1100-6130191/ |website=GameSpot |access-date=2021-12-22 |date=2005-08-31 |archive-date=19 November 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211119163814/https://www.gamespot.com/articles/bedingfield-bonds-with-ea/1100-6130191/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

The development team had full access to MGM's collection of reference material for the film, which helped to recapture its 1960s setting.<ref name=Torres/> The game uses washed-out [[Photographic_print_toning#Sepia_toning|sepia tones]] to match the look of the film,<ref name=OXM>{{cite magazine |title=From Russia With Love preview |url=http://www.computerandvideogames.com/article.php?id=120956 |magazine=[[Official Xbox Magazine]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070506223411/http://www.computerandvideogames.com/article.php?id=120956 |archive-date=2007-05-06 |date=2005-06-24}}</ref> and level designs were based on Bond film sets created by production designer [[Ken Adam]]. The game's art director, Dave Carson, said it was challenging to match the film's time period: "The movie takes place primarily in [[Istanbul]], which offers few '60s-specific images. We used '60s clothing and hairstyles wherever possible".<ref name=GSpy/> The team visited the game's real-life locations, such as [[Big Ben]], to take reference photos.<ref name=Torres/> The game's soundtrack was composed by [[Christopher Lennertz]] and recorded at [[Abbey Road Studios]] in [[London]].<ref name=Virtue>{{cite web |last=Virtue |first=Graeme |title=For better or worse, From Russia With Love was vintage Bond |url=https://www.eurogamer.net/articles/2015-10-25-for-better-or-worse-from-russia-with-love-was-vintage-bond |website=[[Eurogamer]] |access-date=2021-12-22 |date=2015-10-25 |archive-date=22 December 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211222203239/https://www.eurogamer.net/articles/2015-10-25-for-better-or-worse-from-russia-with-love-was-vintage-bond |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Zelfden |first=Alex Van |title=Quantum of Solace: Behind the Music of the Game |url=https://www.ign.com/articles/2008/11/14/quantum-of-solace-behind-the-music-of-the-game |website=IGN |access-date=2021-12-22 |date=2008-11-14 |archive-date=23 December 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211223000104/https://www.ign.com/articles/2008/11/14/quantum-of-solace-behind-the-music-of-the-game |url-status=live }}</ref>

The game was completed on 20 October 2005.<ref name=Gold/><ref>{{cite web |last=Adams |first=David |title=From Russia With Gold |url=https://www.ign.com/articles/2005/10/20/from-russia-with-gold |website=IGN |access-date=2021-12-22 |date=2005-10-20 |archive-date=19 November 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211119163822/https://www.ign.com/articles/2005/10/20/from-russia-with-gold |url-status=live }}</ref> In North America, it was released for the [[PlayStation 2]] and [[Xbox (console)|Xbox]] on 1 November 2005, followed by a [[GameCube]] release two weeks later.<ref>{{cite web |last=Adams |first=David |title=From Russia to Stores |url=https://www.ign.com/articles/2005/11/01/from-russia-to-stores |website=IGN |access-date=2021-12-22 |date=2005-11-01 |archive-date=19 November 2021 ''From Russia with Love'' received "mixed or average" reviews from critics, according to [[review aggregator]] website [[Metacritic]].<ref name="MCXBOX" /><ref name="MCGC" /><ref name="MCPS2" /><ref name="MCPSP" /> Many points were given to the enhanced graphics and play difficulty. ''[[The Times]]'' gave it a score of four stars out of five and stated that "It's enough to make you toss your [[trilby]] on to a hat-rack in delight."<ref name="Times">{{cite news|url=http://entertainment.timesonline.co.uk/article/0,,18589-1989733,00.html |title=From Russia With Love |last=Kendall |first=Nigel |newspaper=[[The Times]] |date=2006-01-21 |access-date=2013-12-07 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060929063945/http://entertainment.timesonline.co.uk/article/0%2C%2C18589-1989733%2C00.html |archive-date=2006-09-29 |url-status=dead }}</ref> However, ''[[Maxim (magazine)|Maxim]]'' gave it a score of six out of ten and stated that though the game was challenging, "it's also sometimes pedestrian, with a host of uninspired levels and dim bad guys ruining what could have been the triumphant return of 007."<ref name="Maxim">{{cite magazine|url=http://www.maxim.com/gaming/russia-with-love|title=From Russia With Love|last=Semel|first=Paul|magazine=[[Maxim (magazine)|Maxim]]|date=2005-11-01|access-date=2013-12-07|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://archive.today/20131207171136/http://www.maxim.com/gaming/russia-with-love|archive-date=2013-12-07}}</ref> Within three months of its release, it had sold approximately 277,000 copies.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2006/02/06/technology/06game.html?_r=1&pagewanted=print&oref=slogin|title=Wave of Video Game Fatigue Afflicts Sales, Not Thumbs – New York Times|newspaper=[[The New York Times]]|date=2006-02-06|access-date=2008-03-30|first=Robert|last=Levine|archive-date=25 February 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120225184529/http://www.nytimes.com/2006/02/06/technology/06game.html?_r=1&pagewanted=print&oref=slogin|url-status=live}}</ref>

In 2014, Schofield expressed disappointment that the game was not rated higher.<ref>{{cite web |last=Robinson |first=Martin |title=The Sledgehammer effect: 'We want to change Call of Duty' |url=https://www.eurogamer.net/articles/2014-09-05-the-sledgehammer-effect-we-want-to-change-this-thing |website=Eurogamer |access-date=2021-12-22 |date=2014-09-12 |archive-date=23 December 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211223000104/https://www.eurogamer.net/articles/2014-09-05-the-sledgehammer-effect-we-want-to-change-this-thing |url-status=live }}</ref> Director [[Michael Condrey]] said, "It was a good game, but we didn't have enough time or resources to really deliver on the vision we wanted for it".<ref>{{cite web |last=Leone |first=Matt |title=The plan to reinvent Call of Duty |url=http://www.polygon.com/a/call-of-duty-cover |website=Polygon |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141028030741/http://www.polygon.com/a/call-of-duty-cover |archive-date=2014-10-28 |date=2014}}</ref> In 2015, Graeme Virtue of ''[[Eurogamer]]'' called the game a "respectful tribute to the formative years of the character", concluding, "It might have ended up a rather haphazard game – with an utterly superfluous [[Natasha Bedingfield]] cameo – but ''From Russia with Love'' remains a fitting cultural artefact to commemorate what will presumably be both EA and Connery's final Bond swan song".<ref name=Virtue/>
